context:
Reuse, do not invent. The framework already has the right shapes — the
bypass adapters just don't consult them. Concretely:

- DataSource extension follows the same idiom DataSourceResolver already
  uses for table_formats: default factory + injection at resolve() time
  so all three providers (BenchmarkTablesSource, BenchmarkImplTablesSource,
  ManifestFileSource) yield the same shape.
- resolve_csv_dialect() precedence (manifest > benchmark > defaults)
  mirrors how table_formats already work: manifest is authoritative,
  benchmark attributes are fallback for legacy paths.
- prepare_local_load_file() is a thin wrapper around the existing
  CompressionHandler family; it does not duplicate that logic, it
  composes it with TPC-specific transforms.
- Adapter migration follows the working-tree pattern from singlestore.py
  that already replaced ZstdCompressor with CompressionManager — but lifts
  ONE level higher to FileFormatRegistry.get_compression_handler().
- Sequential migration with hard gates: SingleStore is the canary because
  it has the most band-aids and the most stress-test coverage. If
  SingleStore goes green, the same pattern works for the others.

Reference implementations to copy from:
- DuckDB adapter (benchbox/platforms/duckdb.py:784) for canonical
  DataLoader use.
- DelimitedFileHandler (benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py:752) for
  the pattern of consulting compression_handler then schema_inspector
  then row_processor.
description:
Four platform adapters — SingleStore, PostgreSQL, Doris, QuestDB — bypass
``benchbox.platforms.base.data_loading.DataSourceResolver`` and iterate
``benchmark.tables`` directly. They reinvent four primitives that already
exist in the framework, in slightly different ways:

- **Compression**: each hardcodes ``data_file.suffix.lower() == ".zst"`` plus
  a direct ``ZstdCompressor`` call. Gzip is silently ignored.
  ``benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py`` already exposes a full
  ``CompressionHandler`` family (``CompressionHandler`` ABC L521,
  ``GzipHandler`` L537, ``ZstdHandler`` L547, ``NoCompressionHandler`` L604)
  and ``FileFormatRegistry.get_compression_handler()``. None of the four
  bypass adapters use them.
- **Trailing-pipe strip**: PostgreSQL L532–541, SingleStore L536–573,
  QuestDB L1133–1146. Three slightly different inline implementations of the
  same TPC-H rule (.tbl rows end in a literal ``|`` terminator that must be
  stripped; .dat rows can have the same shape but the trailing field is
  semantically NULL and must NOT be stripped).
- **CSV dialect**: each adapter does
  ``getattr(benchmark, "csv_delimiter" / "csv_has_header" /
  "csv_normalize_booleans", default)`` — same pattern, four times.
- **Format detection**: each guesses ``.tbl`` vs ``.csv`` vs ``.parquet``
  from filename suffixes when ``_datagen_manifest.json`` already records the
  canonical format per file via ``ManifestTableEntry.format``.

This work moves those four primitives into base helpers, extends the
manifest metadata schema to carry CSV dialect (delimiter, has_header,
null_marker, normalize_booleans, quote), threads that metadata through
``DataSource``/``DataSourceResolver``, annotates the six CSV-bearing
generators, and migrates all four bypass adapters to consume the
authoritative metadata instead of guessing from filenames.

This replaces band-aid commits a1bc0dba2, d24ced0a3, a7acce14b (plus
uncommitted working-tree edits) which fixed real bugs but landed in the
wrong layer — at the leaf rather than in the framework.

**Decisions baked in (confirmed with user before authoring):**

- Scope: all four bypass adapters in one harmonization effort.
- CSV dialect lives in manifest ``metadata`` (not in a benchmark-instance
  helper). The data-on-disk artifact is the source of truth; generators
  write metadata, adapters read it.

Genuinely platform-specific code that STAYS in adapters: DDL transforms
(FK strip, SHARD KEY/SORT KEY on SingleStore, DUPLICATE KEY/DISTRIBUTED BY
on Doris); dialect-specific LOAD syntax (``OPTIONALLY ENCLOSED BY '"'``,
``NULL DEFINED BY ''``, ``IGNORE 1 LINES``, COPY HEADER, Stream Load HTTP,
REST ingestion); boolean rewrite for STRICT_ALL_TABLES.

anti_patterns.dont: batch all four adapter migrations into one commit
anti_patterns.instead: commit per adapter with the per-platform Docker stress check between each.
anti_patterns.why: if one regresses, the others are stuck behind it

anti_patterns.dont: change DDL transforms (FK strip, SHARD KEY, DUPLICATE KEY)
anti_patterns.why: each platform genuinely needs different DDL and prior audit confirmed intentional divergence

anti_patterns.dont: detect compression by suffix string compare (data_file.suffix.lower() == '.zst')
anti_patterns.why: it silently ignores .gz and any future format

anti_patterns.instead: emit logger.warning naming the unannotated table, fall back to format-derived defaults, keep going.
anti_patterns.why: that breaks every TPC benchmark on day one

anti_patterns.dont: revert prior fix commits (a1bc0dba2, d24ced0a3, a7acce14b)
anti_patterns.instead: move the logic up, don't lose the fix.
anti_patterns.why: the bug fixes themselves were correct, only the layer was wrong

anti_patterns.dont: touch TPC-style generators (tpch, tpcds, ssb, datavault) to add metadata
anti_patterns.instead: annotating them adds noise without information.
anti_patterns.why: resolve_csv_dialect() derives the right defaults from format=='tbl'/'dat'
it duplicates the same logic in three places already and keeps drifting

work_units.notes:
Land the schema extension first; nothing downstream uses it yet, so
rollout is safe.

1. Extend ``DataSource`` (benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py:109)
   with a new field:
      ``table_metadata: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=dict)``
   Default factory keeps every existing caller working unchanged.
2. ``ManifestFileSource._try_manifest_v2()`` (L297) populates
   ``table_metadata`` from ``ConvertedFileEntry.conversion_options`` (or
   the equivalent ``ManifestTableEntry.metadata`` on the v2 read side)
   per table.
3. ``DataSourceResolver.resolve()`` (L486) injects ``table_metadata``
   even when the source is ``BenchmarkTablesSource`` /
   ``BenchmarkImplTablesSource`` — same pattern used today for
   ``table_formats`` via ``read_format_hints`` at L512.
4. Document the standardized metadata keys in
   ``benchbox/utils/datagen_manifest.py`` near the ``add_entry()``
   signature (L208):
      csv_delimiter: str
      csv_has_header: bool
      csv_null_marker: str | None  ('' = empty→NULL; None = no conversion)
      csv_normalize_booleans: bool
      csv_quote: str | None  (defaults to '"' when None)
5. **Decision gate** before merging: write a unit test that calls
   ``DataSourceResolver.resolve()`` against a benchmark + manifest with
   metadata populated and asserts ``table_metadata`` round-trips.
   Then write a SECOND test against a benchmark with NO manifest and
   confirm ``table_metadata == {}`` (default factory) — proves the
   schema change is backwards-compatible for the 25 adapters that
   already use ``DataSourceResolver``.

1. Audit unit tests under tests/unit/platforms/ for any remaining
   tests that mock ``is_tpc_format``/``get_delimiter_for_file``/
   ``detect_compression`` directly. Rewrite to inject ``DataSource``.
2. New integration test
   ``tests/integration/test_manifest_driven_loading.py``: build a
   real ``_datagen_manifest.json`` in a tempdir using
   ``DataGenerationManifest`` with each dialect permutation and
   assert each of the four migrated adapters emits the right
   LOAD/COPY/Stream-Load/REST payload — without inspecting filenames.
3. **Mandatory negative case**: write a manifest where the dialect
   metadata DELIBERATELY contradicts the filename (e.g. a file named
   ``data.csv`` with manifest metadata claiming ``has_header=False``
   and a manifest declaring it format=tbl). Assert the adapter emits
   SQL matching the MANIFEST not the filename. If the adapter still
   emits CSV-shaped SQL, it's still guessing — fail the test.
4. Re-run all four adapters' Docker stress tests once more after the
   test refactor to confirm no regressions slipped in.
work_units.summary: Test rewrites + integration coverage with negative case

work_units.notes:
Add to ``benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py``:

1. ``CsvDialect`` dataclass with fields delimiter (str), has_header
   (bool), null_marker (str | None), normalize_booleans (bool),
   quote (str | None).
2. ``resolve_csv_dialect(data_source, table_name, file_path,
   benchmark) -> CsvDialect`` with this precedence:
     a) manifest metadata (data_source.table_metadata[name]) — wins.
     b) benchmark instance attributes (csv_delimiter, csv_has_header,
        csv_normalize_booleans) — fallback for benchmarks not yet
        annotated.
     c) format-derived defaults via ``get_data_extension(file_path)``
        and ``data_source.table_formats``: .tbl/.dat → delimiter='|',
        has_header=False, null_marker='', normalize_booleans=False;
        .csv → delimiter from get_delimiter_for_file(), has_header
        False, null_marker=None, normalize_booleans=False.
   When falling back to (b) or (c), emit a ``logger.warning`` naming
   the table — surfaces unannotated benchmarks without breaking them.

Unit tests required (create tests/unit/platforms/test_csv_dialect.py):
- manifest metadata wins over benchmark attribute wins over format default.
- benchmark attribute wins over format default when no manifest.
- format-derived defaults correct for .tbl, .dat, and .csv.
- logger.warning emitted on fallback; not emitted when manifest wins.
work_units.summary: CsvDialect dataclass + resolve_csv_dialect() with precedence unit tests

work_units.notes:
Add to ``benchbox/platforms/base/data_loading.py``:

``prepare_local_load_file(file_path, *, dialect, strip_trailing_delim)
-> contextmanager[Path]``:
  - Decompresses via ``FileFormatRegistry.get_compression_handler(file_path)``
    — handles zstd, gzip, etc. uniformly.
  - Strips trailing delim per-line if requested.
  - Rewrites True/False → 1/0 if dialect.normalize_booleans.
  - Writes a temp file in file_path.parent only when transformation
    is required; yields original path otherwise (no spurious copies).
  - Cleans up on exit.

Unit tests required (create tests/unit/platforms/test_prepare_local_load_file.py):
- gzip input decompresses correctly; zstd input decompresses correctly.
- uncompressed pass-through yields original path (no temp file written).
- trailing-pipe stripped only when strip_trailing_delim=True.
- True/False → 1/0 only when dialect.normalize_booleans is True.
- context manager cleans up temp file on exit.

For each generator below, find the ``manifest.add_entry()`` call (or
equivalent ``write_generator_manifest()`` invocation) and pass
``metadata={...}`` matching what the generator actually writes. List
based on grep for ``csv_has_header`` / ``csv_delimiter`` /
``csv_normalize_booleans`` (commit only changes that compile + tests
stay green per generator):

- benchbox/core/nyctaxi/         → has_header=True, null_marker=None
- benchbox/core/tsbs_devops/     → has_header=True
- benchbox/core/flightdata/      → has_header=True
- benchbox/core/vector_search/   → has_header=True
- benchbox/core/clickbench/      → delimiter='|', null_marker=None
- benchbox/core/tpcdi/           → normalize_booleans=True, null_marker=''

TPC-style generators (tpch, tpcds, ssb, datavault) are intentionally
NOT annotated — ``resolve_csv_dialect()`` derives correct defaults
from format=='tbl' / 'dat' via the format-derived fallback. Avoids
touching every TPC generator and keeps the diff scoped.

**Decision gate** per generator: after annotating, run that
benchmark's data generation in a tempdir and load the resulting
``_datagen_manifest.json`` via ``benchbox.core.manifest.io.load_manifest``;
assert each table's metadata round-trips. Don't mark this work unit
done until all six round-trip.
work_units.summary: Annotate CSV-bearing benchmark generators with manifest metadata

work_units.notes:
Sequence within this work unit:

1. Replace the manual ``for table_name, table_path in benchmark.tables.items()``
   loop in ``_load_data_infile`` (singlestore.py:492) with
   ``DataSourceResolver(...).resolve(benchmark, data_dir)``. Iterate
   ``data_source.tables`` and consult ``data_source.table_formats``
   and ``data_source.table_metadata``.
2. For each file, ``dialect = resolve_csv_dialect(data_source, name,
   file, benchmark)`` then ``with prepare_local_load_file(file,
   dialect=dialect, strip_trailing_delim=should_strip_trailing) as
   load_path:`` and use the yielded path in the LOAD DATA SQL.
3. Build the LOAD DATA clauses from dialect: ``IGNORE 1 LINES`` if
   dialect.has_header; ``NULL DEFINED BY '<marker>'`` if
   dialect.null_marker is not None; ``FIELDS TERMINATED BY
   '<dialect.delimiter>' OPTIONALLY ENCLOSED BY '"'`` always (the
   OPTIONALLY ENCLOSED is SingleStore-specific for datavault quoted
   fields and stays).
4. Delete: hand-rolled ``is_zst``/``CompressionManager`` block,
   ``should_strip_trailing`` suffix walk, the
   ``getattr(benchmark, "csv_delimiter")`` /
   ``getattr(benchmark, "csv_has_header")`` /
   ``getattr(benchmark, "csv_normalize_booleans")`` chain, the inline
   temp-file rewrite (now in prepare_local_load_file).
5. Keep: FK strip (``_strip_foreign_keys``), SHARD KEY/SORT KEY
   injection, REFERENCE TABLE for nation/region, lowercase backtick
   quoting, OPTIONALLY ENCLOSED BY '"', Parquet skip-with-warning.
   These are genuinely SingleStore-specific.
